# Payment Method Events

A connected clause that announces payment setup and turns payment-request events into MyOS execution requests. It reads `/paymentDetails` and `/paymentDetails/method` from the document where it executes, including a nested instruction’s own document.

## Automatic behavior

- **`announce`** runs on successful clause initialization. It emits a `Payment Event` with `details` copied from `/paymentDetails`. Its `kind` is `Customer Payment Session Requested` when `/paymentDetails/method` equals `myos-customer` exactly; otherwise it is `Account Payment Instruction Created`. This built-in connection has `once: true`: after it completes, its recorded `fired` flag suppresses subsequent execution through that connection. The flag records announcement execution, not payment completion.
- **`request`** responds to an `Event` matching `kind: Payment Requested`. It emits a `Payment Event` with `kind: MyOS Execution Requested`, `details` copied from `/paymentDetails`, `method` copied from `/paymentDetails/method`, and `request` containing the complete triggering event. This connection has no one-time guard or request-deduplication check, so repeated matching events can produce further requests.

Both actions read payment details when they run. No payment-method default or payment-detail validation is declared. Missing details remain unknown; the alternative announcement name does not establish a valid account payment method. These emissions do not confirm customer-session creation, external execution, or completed payment.

## Configuration

Inherited `bindings.announce` and `bindings.request` can add named connections to these actions. `_automatic` is reserved for the built-in connections. A connection’s `when` defaults to true and skips execution when false; `once` defaults to false unless specified. Its `before` and `after` steps surround the action body.

Optional `parameters.conditions.announce` and `parameters.conditions.request` provide additional execution conditions, each defaulting to true when omitted. A false condition rejects execution with `ACTION_CONDITION_FAILED`; condition entries for unknown actions are rejected during planning.

Changing an installed clause’s configuration requires a new clause key; an unchanged instance may retain its key.
